metadata.fatality_note: Total includes both AI users who died (18) and third-party victims killed by AI users (17: Margaux Whittemore, Suzanne Adams, 8 in Tumbler Ridge mass shooting including stepbrother Emmett Jacobs age 11, Robert Morales 57 and Tiru Chabba 45 in FSU mass shooting, Angela Shellis 45 killed by her son using DeepSeek for weapon selection in Wales, Zamil Limon 27 and Nahida Bristy 27 killed at the University of South Florida after the perpetrator consulted ChatGPT on post-mortem disposal, and two adult men in their 20s killed in Seoul motel rooms after the perpetrator consulted ChatGPT on lethal-dose optimization)
metadata.taxonomy_note: Cases classified by mechanism_type (relational_pathway, cognitive_pathway, instrumental_pathway) and outcome_target (self_harm, violence_against_others)

mechanism_definitions.relational_pathway: Emotional dependency, parasocial attachment, or companion relationship contributed to psychological deterioration and lethal outcome
mechanism_definitions.cognitive_pathway: AI validated, reinforced, or amplified delusional, psychotic, or disordered thinking leading to lethal action
mechanism_definitions.instrumental_pathway: AI provided operational assistance, tactical information, or capability that enabled lethal violence as a tool/resource

metadata.verification_standard: Court documents, multiple independent news sources, or official government acknowledgment

statistics.deaths_by_year_note: Counts incidents per year (date of index event). 2024 corrected from 2 to 3 in v3.4.0 to match the 2024 records in the incidents array — prior count was a pre-existing off-by-one. 2025 raised from 14 to 16 in v3.5.0 with the addition of Christian Faith Madison (June 9, 2025) and Alice Carrier (July 2, 2025). 2026 includes Gangbuk-gu motel poisonings (January 28, 2026), Tumbler Ridge mass shooting (February 10, 2026), and University of South Florida double homicide (April 16, 2026).

third_party_victims.breakdown: Whittemore (32), Suzanne Adams (83), Tumbler Ridge 8 victims (mother age 39, stepbrother age 11, education assistant age 39, 5 students ages 12-13), FSU 2 victims (Robert Morales 57, Tiru Chabba 45), Angela Shellis (45, Wales — killed by son following DeepSeek weapon-selection consultation), USF 2 victims (Zamil Limon 27, Nahida Bristy 27 — killed by perpetrator who consulted ChatGPT on post-mortem disposal), Gangbuk-gu Seoul 2 victims (unidentified men in their 20s, killed January 28 and February 9, 2026 — perpetrator queried ChatGPT about lethal sleeping-pill doses; ChatGPT warned her of respiratory-failure death risk and advised calling 119, but the logs were later used forensically by prosecutors as evidence of premeditated murder intent)

instrumental_pathway_casualties.note: FSU (April 17, 2025): 2 killed, 5 wounded, perpetrator alive and awaiting trial. Tumbler Ridge (February 10, 2026): 8 killed + shooter, 2 wounded. Roberts/Shellis (October 23, 2025, Wales): 1 killed (mother), perpetrator convicted of murder. Gangbuk-gu Seoul motel poisonings (indicted period December 14, 2025 – February 9, 2026): 2 killed (January 28 and February 9, 2026), 1 wounded (December 2025 victim survived); perpetrator arrested February 11, indicted on murder charges February 19, 2026. AI's role here is forensic-evidence rather than operational: ChatGPT warned her of respiratory-failure death risk; the logs proved premeditation. University of South Florida double homicide (April 16, 2026): 2 killed, perpetrator indicted May 7, 2026 with death penalty sought.

statistics.minors_percentage_all_incidents_note: Minors affected including survived attempts (6) over incidents with an identified individual AI user (21 of 24; excludes the FSU, Gangbuk-gu, and USF third-party-victim records). Denominator made explicit in v3.5.0.

additional_context.docket_caption: State of Florida v. Ikner, Phoenix
additional_context.docket_court: Leon County Circuit Court, 2nd Judicial Circuit of Florida
additional_context.regulatory_significance: First US state attorney general criminal investigation directly targeting an AI company's responsibility for a mass-casualty event; subpoenas seek internal policies on user threats of harm and law enforcement referral protocols. As of April 27–28, 2026 the investigation was expanded to cover a second Florida incident — the April 2026 USF double homicide — making it the first AG investigation to add a second AI-implicated predicate.
additional_context.criminal_investigation_expansion: AG Uthmeier announced April 27–28, 2026 (one week after opening) that the OpenAI criminal investigation would expand to include the University of South Florida double homicide (Hisham Abugharbieh). Trigger: Tampa prosecutors disclosed Abugharbieh's ChatGPT queries about body disposal (April 13) and firearm use/detection (April 19). Florida Politics characterized the move as 'broadening' the existing investigation rather than opening a separate one. No specific OpenAI public statement on the expansion has been located.
additional_context.openai_response: Spokesperson Kate Waters: 'Last year's mass shooting at Florida State University was a tragedy, but ChatGPT is not responsible for this terrible crime.'
additional_context.uthmeier_quote: 'My prosecutors have looked at this and they've told me, if it was a person on the other end of that screen, we would be charging them with murder. We cannot have AI bots that are advising people on how to kill others.'
additional_context.trial_status: Trial set for October 19, 2026; jury selection November 3. Phoenix Ikner made his first in-person court appearance on May 26, 2026 (red jumpsuit); Circuit Judge Lance Neff (retained by FL Supreme Court Chief Justice Carlos Muñiz order April 7, 2026 despite Neff's appointment to the First DCA) deferred ruling on the defense's delay request. Judge Neff issued a written scheduling order on May 28, 2026 tracking the State's proposed deadlines without granting the delay: guilt-phase witness disclosure June 1, 2026; penalty-phase witnesses July 1; rebuttal witnesses August 1. October 19, 2026 trial date confirmed unchanged. Late-June 2026 hearing scheduled to address all pending motions including the defense's delay request.
additional_context.message_volume: 13,000+ messages with ChatGPT over more than one year; 200+ entered as evidence
additional_context.civil_docket_caption: Joshi v. OpenAI Foundation et al.
additional_context.civil_docket_court: U.S. District Court, Northern District of Florida, Tallahassee Division
additional_context.civil_plaintiff: Vandana Joshi (widow of Tiru Chabba, 45 — Aramark Collegiate Hospitality regional VP killed in the shooting)
additional_context.civil_defendants: OpenAI (as the Foundation et al.) and Phoenix Ikner (as co-defendant)
additional_context.civil_legal_representation: Osborne, Francis & Pettis + Strom Law Firm + Bannister, Wyatt & Stalvey
additional_context.civil_claims: Negligence, gross negligence, three strict products liability counts (defective design, negligent design, failure to warn), negligent entrustment, battery (against Ikner), Florida wrongful death
additional_context.civil_complaint_allegations: ChatGPT allegedly told Ikner a shooting would attract more national media attention 'if children are involved' (even 2–3 child victims would draw greater coverage); ChatGPT identified firearms from photos Ikner uploaded and provided instructions on loading and operation; ChatGPT discussed busiest times at FSU's Student Union as part of target selection; conversations allegedly continued until minutes before the shooting began
additional_context.civil_legal_significance: First federal wrongful death civil action filed by a victim family in an AI-implicated mass-shooting case; tests Florida products-liability law as applied to a generative AI system; ninth+ wrongful death suit against OpenAI as of May 2026 and the first invoking a federal-court forum for a chatbot-mass-shooting theory (most prior OpenAI wrongful death suits sit in CA Superior or N.D. Cal.)
additional_context.presiding_judge: Circuit Judge Lance Neff (Leon County Circuit Court, 2nd Judicial Circuit of Florida); retained as 'acting circuit judge' for the Ikner case by Florida Supreme Court Chief Justice Carlos Muñiz order dated April 7, 2026, after Neff's appointment to the First DCA
additional_context.prosecution_team: State Attorney Jack Campbell (personally prosecuting the case)
additional_context.may_2026_in_person_hearing: May 26, 2026 — first in-person court appearance by Ikner since arrest; defense argued the volume of electronic discovery (explicitly citing 'Ikner's alleged ChatGPT conversation logs and the Florida AG's parallel criminal investigation into OpenAI') made the case 'complicated' and meeting the State's proposed pre-trial deadlines 'virtually impossible.' Defense quote (Johnson): 'We could not be ready to list our experts by the State's proposed dates simply because our investigation is not complete.' Judge Neff deferred ruling on the delay request.
additional_context.may_2026_scheduling_order: May 28, 2026 — written scheduling order. Tracks State's proposed deadlines: June 1 (guilt-phase witnesses), July 1 (penalty-phase witnesses), August 1 (rebuttal witnesses). October 19, 2026 trial date confirmed unchanged. Late-June hearing announced to address all pending motions, including the defense's delay request.
additional_context.defense_chatgpt_logs_discovery_reference: The May 26, 2026 in-person appearance is the first public acknowledgment by defense counsel that the AI conversation evidence is a contested feature of trial preparation — defense counsel Randall Johnson explicitly cited Ikner's ChatGPT logs and the parallel FL AG criminal investigation into OpenAI as factors complicating discovery. Whether the defense has reviewed the Joshi/Chabba civil-case discovery (which contains detailed allegations about specific ChatGPT exchanges, filed May 10, 2026) or is relying solely on the criminal docket's 200+ AI messages already in evidence is not publicly known. This is a methodologically significant moment: AI conversation evidence is shifting from prosecution exhibit to contested discovery scope in a death-penalty criminal trial.

The pre-crime ChatGPT consultation on April 13 was about post-mortem disposal logistics, not about attack planning in the conventional sense — this is a meaningful departure from the FSU (target selection, casualty maximization) and Tumbler Ridge (months-long ideation reinforcement) patterns, and is documented as such rather than collapsed into a new taxonomy bucket

congressional_hearings.topic: Examining the harm of AI chatbots

investigations.target: OpenAI (OpenAI Global LLC; OpenAI Foundation; OpenAI OpCo LLC; OpenAI Group PBC; OpenAI Holdings LLC) and CEO Samuel H. Altman, personally
investigations.scope: Statewide civil action over ChatGPT's alleged safety failures; predicated on the April 2025 FSU mass shooting (Ikner's ChatGPT logs cited as central evidence), the Adam Raine suicide (April 2025), and the Tumbler Ridge mass shooting (February 2026). Grew out of the AG's prior pre-April 2026 civil investigation.
investigations.court: Circuit Court of the Tenth Judicial Circuit, Highlands County, Florida
investigations.claims: Ten counts: four under the Florida Deceptive and Unfair Trade Practices Act (FDUTPA), two common-law negligence, two strict product liability, one fraudulent misrepresentation, one public nuisance
investigations.relief_sought: Civil penalties up to $10,000 per violation; injunctive relief; compensatory damages; disgorgement of profits; a court order barring collection of data from users under 13 without parental consent. AG characterized OpenAI's exposure as 'potentially up to billions of dollars.'
investigations.note: First US state civil lawsuit against OpenAI and the first state civil action to name an AI company CEO (Altman) personally liable for user harms. Runs parallel to — not in lieu of — the still-active Florida AG criminal investigation (see separate entry). Distinct from the federal Joshi v. OpenAI wrongful-death suit, which also arises from the FSU shooting.
investigations.source: Florida AG press release and filed-stamped complaint PDF (myfloridalegal.com); NPR; NBC News; TechCrunch; CNBC; Variety (all June 1, 2026)

investigations.scope: Potential criminal liability in the April 2025 FSU mass shooting; subpoenas issued for OpenAI policies and internal training materials related to user threats of harm and law-enforcement cooperation dating back to March 2024
investigations.key_quote: 'My prosecutors have looked at this and they've told me, if it was a person on the other end of that screen, we would be charging them with murder.' — AG James Uthmeier
investigations.note: First US state attorney general criminal investigation directly targeting an AI company's responsibility for a mass-casualty event

investigations.agency: Pennsylvania Office of Attorney General (Shapiro administration)
investigations.scope: Allegation that Character.AI bots unlawfully held themselves out as licensed medical professionals in Pennsylvania — a Character.AI bot named 'Emilie' described itself to investigators as a licensed psychiatrist in PA and the UK, provided a fake PA medical license number, offered to conduct mental health assessments, and accumulated approximately 45,500 interactions as of April 17, 2026
investigations.relief_sought: Preliminary injunction requiring Character.AI to cease allowing bots to represent themselves as licensed medical or mental health professionals in PA
investigations.note: First-of-its-kind state-AG enforcement action by a governor framing AI chatbot conduct as unlicensed practice of a licensed profession (medicine/psychiatry); the same unlicensed-practice-of-medicine theory was advanced privately one week later in Turner-Scott v. OpenAI Foundation et al. (SF County Superior, May 12, 2026) for Sam Nelson
investigations.source: Pennsylvania Governor's Office press release (May 5, 2026); NPR (May 5, 2026); TechCrunch (May 5, 2026); Washington Times / AP feed

investigations.agency: Office of the Privacy Commissioner of Canada (jointly with provincial commissioners of British Columbia, Alberta, and Quebec)
investigations.scope: Finding that OpenAI failed to comply with the Personal Information Protection and Electronic Documents Act (PIPEDA) in training ChatGPT — used Canadians' personal information without adequate consent
investigations.outcome: OpenAI required to implement corrective measures; specific remedies not publicly detailed in available sources
investigations.relationship_to_tumbler_ridge: Parallel regulatory track to the RCMP criminal investigation into the Tumbler Ridge mass shooting (incident 2026-02-CA-001) and the NDCA $1B civil litigation filed April 29, 2026 — not a criminal finding tied to the shooting itself
investigations.note: First formal Canadian government determination finding OpenAI in violation of law
investigations.source: Office of the Privacy Commissioner of Canada, PIPEDA Findings #2026-002 (https://www.priv.gc.ca/en/opc-actions-and-decisions/investigations/investigations-into-businesses/2026/pipeda-2026-002-overview/)

investigations.agency: 42-state attorney general coalition (led by New York AG Letitia James)
investigations.scope: Sycophancy documentation, child-safety records, consumer and health data practices, advertising practices, and user-retention/engagement mechanics; served four days after OpenAI's confidential S-1 filing. First multistate enforcement action to name model sycophancy explicitly as a harm vector.

legislation.name: GUARD Act
legislation.full_name: Guidelines for User Age-verification and Responsible Dialogue Act of 2025
key_provisions: Prohibits minors from accessing AI companion chatbots
Requires disclosure that chatbot is AI at start of each conversation and at 30-minute intervals
Criminal penalties (up to $100,000) for bots that solicit or encourage minors to engage in sexual conduct, suicide, or violence

legislation.name: California SB 243
legislation.description: First-in-the-nation AI chatbot safeguards law requiring companion chatbot operators to implement safeguards and providing families private right of action
